content:
Talia Benson: Retro thread for Unit Econ Dashboard v1 build. Drop thoughts async: what went well, what didn’t, and what we want to change for v1.1. If you have concrete action items + owners, please include.

Dylan Brooks: Overall: shipped a cross-functional metric + dashboard in ~11 wks with Finance signoff. That’s a win. Biggest pain points were (1) metric definition churn early and (2) data quality surprises late (streaming tokens, region nulls). We should do earlier “data parity” gates next time.

Laura Bennett: +1 on “Finance signoff” being a real milestone. What went well: we ended up with a methodology doc + reconciliation report that Finance can cite. What didn’t: we didn’t have a stable answer for “why dashboard != billing” until very late, which made exec comms hard.

Rishi Malhotra: Specifically: reconciliation was blocked on (a) day boundary/timezone differences (Finance reports by PT day, pipeline was UTC hour buckets) and (b) rate card versioning assumptions. We now have a path, but v1.1 should make the version used more visible in the UI (even if internal-only).

Logan Wright: Telemetry side: big win was converging on canonical dimensions (model_id/model_version, region_normalized, customer_tier, streaming flag, quant_profile). Nadia/Mei team moved fast.

Logan Wright: Biggest miss: we didn’t have automated checks for “output tokens parity streaming vs non-streaming” from day 1. We relied on spot checks, which meant the undercount escaped until dogfood + customer tickets.

Nadia Rahman: Agree. The streaming path had multiple emit points and one code path dropped final token counts on tool-call + truncation combos. Tests were added, but we should add a canary dataset + golden queries that run daily and compare distributions (streaming/non-streaming, by route).

Caleb Johnson: Data quality checks: what worked: completeness alerts on missing hour partitions + missing dimension coverage caught real issues (ingestion lag incident, region mapping null drop). What didn’t: alert noise first 48h was high, we tuned thresholds reactively.

Caleb Johnson: v1.1 idea: add a “confidence / coverage indicator” computed per slice (e.g., % rows with unknown region/tier, late arrivals). If confidence is low, dashboard should warn and/or hide comparisons. People will otherwise screenshot wrong numbers.

Allison Grant: SRE/observability: the SLO doc + runbook links in alert payloads were clutch. Oncall was able to self-serve backfill + verify.

Allison Grant: But… we treated the warehouse like an infinite resource during backfill week. We overloaded it and caused timeouts for other analytics. Need a throttled backfill mode + maintenance window coordination in the runbook.

Sean Gallagher: Adding: for v1 we had alerts, but we didn’t have an explicit “stop the line” gate. We kept shipping UI changes while pipeline was unstable, which confused Finance users (“it changed again”). Suggest: define launch gates for v1.1 (freshness SLO green, reconciliation within tolerance, no P0 open) and freeze UI/metric changes during signoff window.

Chloe Martin: Console backend: API caching vs freshness thread was painful but landed well (separate live-ish view vs finance-stable view). What went well: caching + rate limits prevented someone from accidentally DDOSing the view with wide group_by.

Chloe Martin: What didn’t: our query API contract was a bit too flexible; some group_by combos are expensive and not that useful. For v1.1 I’d like to constrain + provide “supported breakdowns” explicitly, and move some heavy queries to pre-aggregations.

Mei Lin: Warehouse/views: pre-aggregation saved us. Once we partitioned correctly, top-N + time series became usable.

Mei Lin: Miss: region normalization mapping table didn’t handle unknown/null consistently at first, which dropped rows silently. We fixed, but we should enforce “unknown region” bucket at ingestion + have a hard fail if the drop rate exceeds threshold.

Felix Schneider: Dashboard/UI: filters + drilldown nav tested well in dogfood. People immediately used model+region to find outliers.

Felix Schneider: UX miss: blended cost vs marginal cost confusion. We had tooltip copy but it didn’t prevent misreads. In v1.1 we should add a small “How to interpret” panel + link to methodology + show what’s included (idle allocation, overhead) for the selected tier.

Alicia Perez: +1. Also formatting: we got late feedback about rounding + unit labeling. People were comparing noise. v1.1 should adopt the viz guideline defaults everywhere: $/1M output tokens to 2 decimals (or 3 if <1), and show delta bands only when confidence is high.

Marissa Cole: Product: the core promise landed: “find cost outliers fast.” We saw multiple eng investigations triggered by the top-N tables.

Marissa Cole: What didn’t: scope churn. We kept debating adding model-version drilldown + saved views while pipeline was still in flux. For v1.1 I’d prefer we sequence: (1) trust + correctness upgrades, (2) then additional drilldowns + UX convenience.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Access controls: feature flag + RBAC was straightforward technically, but we didn’t have a clear initial allowlist owner, so internal support tickets piled up. v1.1: define an access policy doc + a self-serve request workflow (still internal), and audit log review cadence.

Marcus Lin: Security review note: we did the right thing by avoiding customer-identifiable drilldowns. Please keep that line. For v1.1, if we add “top customers” internally, it needs a separate gated view and clear legal/finance signoff. Default should remain aggregated by tier/region/model.

Cole Summers: Cost attribution: biggest win was aligning on allocation basis + idle treatment and capturing it in ADR w/ versioning. Biggest pain: rate card updates are operationally messy. We need a process: when rate card changes, pipeline should tag computations with rate_card_version and UI should surface it.

Jada Williams: Architecture: having ADR-034 early helped stop bikeshedding, but it still took too long to settle. Suggest: start v1.1 with an “assumption lock” meeting: definition, timezone/day boundary, rate card versioning, overhead policy. If something changes mid-flight, it gets a version bump (no silent changes).

Talia Benson: Pulling action items from thread (please react/confirm owners):
1) Add daily parity checks for output token metering (streaming vs non-streaming) + golden queries; include tool-call/truncation cases — owner: Nadia / Logan?
2) Implement confidence/coverage indicator per slice + UI warning behavior — owner: Caleb + Felix + Alicia
3) Backfill throttling + maintenance window guidance; update runbook and automation — owner: Allison + Mei
4) Make rate_card_version + methodology version visible in UI/export; document update process — owner: Cole + Rishi + Chloe
5) Define v1.1 launch gates + freeze window for Finance signoff — owner: Sean + Laura + Talia
6) Constrain API supported breakdowns + add pre-aggregations for expensive group_bys — owner: Chloe + Mei
7) Improve “blended vs marginal” education in UI (panel/tooltips) — owner: Marissa + Alicia

Dylan Brooks: For #1 owner: Nadia to drive tests + canary, Logan to integrate into pipeline checks. :thumbsup:

Nadia Rahman: Works for me. I’ll draft the test matrix + add a “known tricky paths” list (tool calls, streaming cancel, truncation) and we can wire into canary.

Laura Bennett: For #5, Finance is in. Please make the tolerance explicit (e.g., reconciliation within X% or $Y at QTD level). Otherwise we’ll re-litigate.

Sean Gallagher: +1. I’ll propose thresholds based on what we saw in v1 and what’s practical (and we can tighten over time).

Talia Benson: Great. I’ll turn these into v1.1 kickoff agenda + track in Linear. Keep adding notes if you think of more.
